newsitem.title: USA: Motown Records CEO resigns, Polygram says.
newsitem.headline: Motown Records CEO resigns, Polygram says.

text.p: Polygram Holding Inc. said Monday that Andre Harrell has resigned from his post as president and chief executive officer of Motown Records, effective immediately.
While the recruitment for a new Motown president is conducted, day-to-day operations will be overseen by its chairman, Clarence Avant, and Motown's senior staff, Polygram said.
Motown's current roster has over 25 artists, including Boyz II Men, which will release a new album this fall, Diana Ross, Stevie Wonder, Queen Latifah, Zhane, and the new group 98 Degrees.
Motown, one of the legendary labels in the music business, was founded in Detroit in 1959 by Berry Gordy Jr.

Motown helped launch the careers of the Jackson Five, The Supremes, the Temptations, Lionel Richie and the Commodores, Smokey Robinson & The Miracles, and The Four Tops. Their works are included in Motown's back catalogue of over 30,000 records.
